name: The gazetteer
note: Seventy SITE events. Each one is a place somebody dug, with the excavation as the evidence line. Priority went to the eras the density check was failing: Second Urbanisation, Mauryan, Classical, Gupta and Regional Kingdoms.

events.title: Bhita on the Yamuna: a town excavated street by street
events.evidence: Marshall's 1911-12 excavation, which exposed a complete street frontage with shops, houses and a guild hall.
events.note: One of the few Indian sites dug as a town plan rather than a mound section.

events.title: Atranjikhera crosses into Northern Black Polished Ware
events.evidence: A four-period sequence from Ochre Coloured Pottery through Painted Grey Ware to NBPW, with iron slag from the PGW level up.

events.title: Sravasti's rampart is raised, enclosing four hundred hectares
events.evidence: The surviving earthwork circuit, and the Jetavana monastery within it.

events.title: Vaishali: the Licchavi capital, and a republic with a wall
events.evidence: The Raja Vishal ka Garh mound, the Licchavi stupa, and the Pali canon's descriptions of the assembly hall.
events.note: A republic that fortified itself is a republic that expected a siege.

events.title: Champa on the Ganga: Anga's capital and the eastern river gate
events.evidence: Excavation at Champanagar showing a rampart and moat, and the Anguttara Nikaya's list of the six great cities.

events.title: Ujjain's mud rampart and moat enclose the Malwa route
events.evidence: The Garh Kalika mound's rampart section, radiocarbon dated, with NBPW above.

events.title: Mathura on the Yamuna becomes a city
events.evidence: NBPW levels beneath the Kushan city, and the Jain and Buddhist textual record of a Surasena capital.

events.title: Kausambi's eastern gate and the Ghositarama monastery
events.evidence: G. R. Sharma's excavation of the defences and the monastery complex named in the Pali canon.

events.title: Prakash and Bahal: the Tapi valley enters the iron age town network
events.evidence: Deccan College excavations showing Jorwe levels overlain by iron-using occupation.

events.title: Sisupalgarh's grid is laid out with eight gateways
events.evidence: The surviving rampart square with its paired gateways, and the laterite pillar array at the centre.

events.title: Pataliputra's timber palisade, as Megasthenes described it
events.evidence: Waterlogged sal-wood palisade timbers excavated at Bulandi Bagh, matching the Greek account of a wooden wall with 570 towers.
events.note: A Greek ambassador described it, and the wood is still there.

events.title: Kumrahar's eighty-pillared hall
events.evidence: The polished sandstone pillar bases in situ, and the wooden platform beneath them.

events.title: Bairat: a circular Buddhist shrine and two Ashokan edicts
events.evidence: The circular brick chaitya foundation with a stupa at its centre, and the Bhabru and Bairat inscriptions.

events.title: The Barabar caves are cut and polished to a mirror
events.evidence: The Lomas Rishi and Sudama caves themselves, with dedicatory inscriptions to the Ajivikas.
events.note: Granite polished so fine it still returns an echo. Nobody has fully explained how.

events.title: Taxila's Bhir Mound: an unplanned city under Mauryan rule
events.evidence: Marshall's stratigraphy at Bhir Mound, with Mauryan punch-marked coin hoards.

events.title: Dhauli and Jaugada: edict rocks placed where Kalinga could read them
events.evidence: The two separate Kalinga edicts, cut at the sites of the conquered province's administration.

events.title: Sannati on the Bhima: a Mauryan edict found reused as a temple floor slab
events.evidence: The Ashokan separate edicts recovered from the Chandralamba temple, published in 1989.
events.note: Found in 1986 under a goddess. Edicts are still turning up.

events.title: Sisupalgarh at its height under Mauryan administration
events.evidence: Rouletted ware, NBPW and a coin sequence from the rampart trenches.

events.title: Mahasthangarh's rampart and its famine-relief order
events.evidence: The Brahmi limestone plaque ordering grain from the state store, and the rampart it was found beside.

events.title: Sohgaura's copper plate is fixed at a storehouse
events.evidence: The copper plaque itself, showing three storehouses in relief above the order.

events.title: Arikamedu: a fishing village becomes a Roman trading station
events.evidence: Wheeler's 1945 trench through the warehouse, with Arretine ware, amphora sherds and Roman lamps stratified above local rouletted ware.

events.title: Pattanam on the Periyar, argued to be Muziris
events.evidence: Amphorae, Roman glass, a wharf and a dugout canoe; the identification with Muziris rests on the Peutinger Table and the Periplus.

events.title: Kodumanal's crucible steel furnaces
events.evidence: Slag, crucible fragments and high-carbon steel from the industrial quarter, with Tamil-Brahmi graffiti on the pottery.

events.title: Indian goods reach Berenike and Myos Hormos on the Red Sea
events.evidence: Black pepper, Indian teak ship timbers and Tamil-Brahmi graffiti on storage jars excavated at Berenike.
events.note: A Tamil name scratched on a jar in Egypt is the trade route in one object.

events.title: Sanghol in the Punjab: a Kushan stupa with 117 railing pillars buried in a pit
events.evidence: The 1985 discovery of the dismantled railing, carved in Mathura sandstone and buried intact.

events.title: Sonkh near Mathura: a naga shrine in an unbroken sequence
events.evidence: Härtel's excavation, which produced an apsidal naga temple and a stratigraphy running from PGW to the medieval period.

events.title: Nagarjunakonda: a planned Ikshvaku capital in the Krishna valley
events.evidence: The excavation before the dam flooded the valley, which recorded a citadel, thirty monasteries, a stadium and an amphitheatre.

events.title: Kanheri's hundred and nine caves are cut above the Konkan ports
events.evidence: The cave complex itself, with donative inscriptions naming merchants from Kalyan and Sopara.

events.title: Sopara: the western port that received an Ashokan edict and Roman cargo
events.evidence: The stupa at Nala Sopara, the eighth and ninth rock edict fragments, and the Periplus's Souppara.

events.title: Sisupalgarh is abandoned
events.evidence: The end of the occupation sequence in the rampart trenches, with no destruction layer.

events.title: Ter (Tagara) on the Deccan trade road
events.evidence: Roman glass, ivory, and a brick apsidal shrine; the Periplus names Tagara as an inland market.

events.title: Banavasi under the Chutus: a brick stupa on the Varada
events.evidence: The Chutu Prakrit inscriptions and the brick stupa base beneath the later Madhukeshwara temple.

events.title: Vadgaon-Madhavpur yields a Roman coin hoard and a bath
events.evidence: Excavation near Belgaum producing Roman denarii, a brick tank and Satavahana levels.

events.title: Bhokardan (Bhogavardhana) supplies the ghat trade with ivory
events.evidence: Ivory workshop debris and a plaque comparable to the Pompeii ivory figure.

events.title: Kaveripattinam's brick wharf and warehouse
events.evidence: The wharf structure excavated at Puhar, and the Pattinappalai's description of customs officers stamping bales.

events.title: Bhitargaon: the earliest surviving brick temple with a corbelled tower
events.evidence: The temple itself, with terracotta panels and a true arch in the doorway.

events.title: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh sets the northern plan
events.evidence: The temple's surviving sanctum, panels and plinth, with its four subsidiary shrines.

events.title: Sarnath's workshops produce the seated preaching Buddha
events.evidence: The Dhamek stupa's surroundings and the image workshop debris, with dated pedestal inscriptions.

events.title: Mandsaur: a silk weavers' guild builds and rebuilds a sun temple
events.evidence: The Mandsaur inscription of 473, which records the guild's migration from Lata and its repair of the temple it had built.
events.note: A guild of weavers moved across the country, built a temple, and paid to fix it eighty years later.

events.title: Sirpur on the Mahanadi: a Buddhist and Shaiva city in Dakshina Kosala
events.evidence: The Lakshmana brick temple, the Anandaprabhu vihara, and a market street excavated in the 2000s.

events.title: Valabhi: a port capital whose university drew students from the north
events.evidence: The Maitraka copper-plate grant series, and Yijing's report that Valabhi and Nalanda were the two great schools.

events.title: The Bagh caves are cut and painted on the Narmada
events.evidence: The rock-cut viharas and the surviving mural fragments, now removed to Gwalior.

events.title: Nalanda's plan sets: viharas facing temples across a central walk
events.evidence: The excavated ground plan — eleven monasteries and six temples on a north-south axis — and the seals naming the mahavihara.

events.title: Somapura Mahavihara is built at Paharpur on a cruciform plan
events.evidence: The excavated central shrine and its 177 monastic cells, and Dharmapala's seals.

events.title: Mahasthangarh continues as Pundravardhana's administrative seat
events.evidence: The Gupta-period levels within the rampart and the copper-plate grants issued from the city.

events.title: Devnimori's stupa yields a dated relic casket
events.evidence: The casket inscription giving a regnal year, excavated before the Meshwo dam flooded the site.

events.title: Kausambi's occupation thins and the rampart is not maintained
events.evidence: The upper levels of Sharma's trenches, with no rebuilding above the Gupta floor.

events.title: Aihole: a hundred and twenty-five temples as an architectural laboratory
events.evidence: The temples themselves, which try the apsidal, the flat-roofed, the northern and the southern plan within a few hundred metres.
events.note: Somebody was experimenting, and left the drafts standing.

events.title: Pattadakal builds northern and southern towers side by side
events.evidence: The Virupaksha and Papanatha temples, and the mason's signature inscriptions naming the guilds.

events.title: Ellora's Kailasa is cut downward out of the cliff
events.evidence: The monolith itself and the two hundred thousand tonnes of removed basalt, with Rashtrakuta grants naming the patron.
events.note: Not built. Removed. They started at the top and took the mountain away.

events.title: Elephanta's cave and the Trimurti are cut
events.evidence: The cave itself; the dating rests on style and on a disputed Kalachuri attribution.

events.title: Mahabalipuram's rathas are cut, and left unfinished
events.evidence: The five monoliths, each abandoned at a different stage, which together show the whole method.
events.note: Unfinished work teaches more than finished work.

events.title: Kanchipuram's temple workshops become a school
events.evidence: The Kailasanatha's foundation inscriptions and the sequence of Pallava temples around the city.

events.title: Srirangam's island temple begins its expansion outward
events.evidence: The earliest inscriptions on the inner prakaram walls, and the Alvar hymns that address the site.

events.title: Lalitagiri, Ratnagiri and Udayagiri form the Odishan diamond triangle
events.evidence: The three excavated complexes, with Ratnagiri's monastery doorway and a relic casket from Lalitagiri.

events.title: Martand is built on the Kashmir plateau, facing the valley
events.evidence: The colonnaded courtyard and trefoil arches, and Kalhana's attribution to Lalitaditya.

events.title: Parihasapura: Lalitaditya's new capital, built and then quarried
events.evidence: The stupa base and the vast unmortared blocks, many later carried off for other buildings.

events.title: Dhar and the Malwa uplands under the Paramaras
events.evidence: The Bhojshala inscriptions and the Paramara grant series.

events.title: Osian's temple cluster sets the Maru-Gurjara idiom
events.evidence: Sixteen surviving temples with dated Pratihara-period sculpture.

events.title: Gangaikonda Cholapuram is laid out as a capital, not just a temple
events.evidence: The temple, the six-kilometre Chola Gangam tank, and the palace mound at Maligaimedu.

events.title: The Chola Gangam and the great delta tanks are cut
events.evidence: The surviving bund, and the inscriptions recording tank committees and desilting duties.

events.title: Kumbakonam's temple cluster becomes a delta town of shrines
events.evidence: The Nageswaran and Sarangapani temples and their inscription series.

events.title: Dholavira is reoccupied briefly, and left again
events.evidence: Stage VII at the site: crude round houses built over the ruins of the planned town.
events.note: Somebody came back, lived in the ruins, and left. Nobody knows who.

events.title: Warangal's concentric fort and its four gateways
events.evidence: The granite and earth ramparts and the four freestanding torana gateways still in place.

events.title: Vijayanagara is laid out across seven ranges of hills
events.evidence: The surviving urban core: the royal centre, the sacred centre, the aqueducts and the bazaar streets.

events.title: Vijayanagara's water system supplies a city in a dry granite basin
events.evidence: The Kamalapuram tank, the aqueduct channels and the stepped tank of dressed schist brought from elsewhere.

events.title: Daulatabad is cut into a rock cone and made a capital
events.evidence: The scarped rock face, the spiral tunnel, and the Delhi population that was marched there and back.

events.title: Gaur and Pandua build a Bengal idiom in brick
events.evidence: The Adina mosque at Pandua and the brick and terracotta mosques of Gaur.

events.title: Champaner is built below Pavagadh as a Gujarat capital
events.evidence: The Jama Masjid, the helical stepwells and the surviving town walls.

events.title: Mandu's plateau city and its water architecture
events.evidence: The Jahaz Mahal between two tanks, the Hindola Mahal and the twelve-kilometre wall circuit.

events.title: Srirangapatna is fortified on its river island
events.evidence: The island fort's earliest bastions, later rebuilt under Tipu Sultan.

events.title: Lepakshi's murals are painted on a Vijayanagara ceiling
events.evidence: The Virabhadra temple's painted ceiling, the largest surviving pre-modern mural cycle in south India.

events.title: Masulipatnam becomes the Coromandel's chintz port
events.evidence: Dutch and English factory records, and the kalamkari workshops of the hinterland.

events.title: Fatehpur Sikri is built, occupied, and left within fifteen years
events.evidence: The complete surviving city, and the Mughal chronicles that record its abandonment.
events.note: A capital built from nothing and empty in a generation, most likely for want of water.

events.title: Surat becomes the Mughal empire's sea gate
events.evidence: The customs house records, the English and Dutch factories, and the pilgrim traffic to the Red Sea.

events.title: Hugli, Chinsurah and the Bengal river factories
events.evidence: Portuguese, Dutch, French and Danish factory sites along a forty-kilometre stretch of one river.

events.title: Shahjahanabad is laid out with its bazaar on a canal
events.evidence: The walled city, the Chandni Chowk canal alignment, and the imperial building accounts.

events.title: Srirangapatna falls and the Mysore capital moves
events.evidence: The breach in the north wall, and the East India Company's own account of the storming.
